scope: Native single-host MemX before/after large-index microbenchmark, plus a separate mixed small-object comparator. Not a production allocator superiority claim.

environment.execution: Native outside sandbox; no QEMU; timing phases sequential, no concurrent compilation or tests launched by this agent.

provenance.candidate_revision: Working changes relative to baseline; identify tested heap by SHA256, not the baseline revision.

methodology.untimed_shuffle: Fixed-seed permutation reused cyclically within each query phase; identical for baseline and candidate.
methodology.warmup_semantics: Separate process repetition 0 excluded; does not warm allocator state in later fresh processes.
methodology.run_order: For each population: repetition 0..7; before/after on even repetitions, after/before on odd.
methodology.checks: Exit zero, 1638400000 checksum, interior misses zero, shrink preserves pointer and two touched payload bytes, post-shrink sizes, all frees succeed.
methodology.units: All timings in ns/op. MAD is median absolute deviation across process-level phase averages, not operation-level tail latency.

memory.category: Calculated requested bucket-array bytes, not RSS; no bucket array in baseline
memory.heap_struct_measurement: Clang 22 record-layout dump with current x86-64 glibc headers; one old atomic counter was removed while adding two table counters.
memory.peak_growth_bucket_formula: old B plus new 2B pointers = 3B*sizeof(pointer), excluding records, allocator overhead, and mappings
memory.tests: Structural accounting tested for growth, shrink, allocation failure, zero activity statistics, and empty-table recreation.

object_footprint.tool: GNU size (text column includes read-only data)

mixed_small_comparison.scope: Does not exercise large-index path; regression and competitor check only. MemX allocator APIs compiled from same workload source; system and mimalloc use the exact same workload executable.

mimalloc.build: GNU 16.2.1, Release -O3 -DNDEBUG, MI_OVERRIDE=ON, MI_SECURE=OFF, MI_DEBUG_FULL=OFF, shared library
mimalloc.override_verification: LD_DEBUG=bindings confirmed malloc/calloc/realloc/free in workload resolved to this mimalloc library; verification run not timed.

api_contracts.before: Conventional unchecked MemX free/realloc, baseline heap
api_contracts.after: Conventional unchecked MemX free/realloc, candidate heap
api_contracts.checked: Candidate MemX checked free/realloc sensitivity result
api_contracts.mimalloc: Same system workload with mimalloc preload; slot/order bookkeeping also uses selected malloc implementation.

mixed_small_comparison.run_order: Rotating five-variant order [before, after, checked, glibc, mimalloc]; start index repetition modulo 5; repetition 0 excluded.
mixed_small_comparison.interpretation: Candidate is slower than mimalloc at the median in this workload. Mimalloc is highly variable/bimodal (86.054..620.895 ns/op), so do not infer a universal ratio. Candidate vs baseline median difference is within each run set's MAD; no proven small-path improvement.

validation.clang_asan_ubsan: 8/8 passed outside sandbox with leak detection enabled
validation.clang_tsan: memx_heap_test passed outside sandbox including new concurrent large churn
validation.gcc_x86_32: 8/8 passed outside sandbox; initial sandbox run SIGSYS is excluded as environment restriction
validation.qemu_mips32: 8/8 CTest passed; Python tool test runs on host
validation.qemu_ppc64le: 8/8 CTest passed; Python tool test runs on host
validation.qemu_sparc64: 8/8 CTest passed; Python tool test runs on host
validation.fault_injection: calloc first table, growth, realloc metadata and growth failure preservation/recovery, shrink failure and final release

limitations: One host, uncontrolled frequency/thermals/background activity; no confidence intervals or per-operation p95/p99 claims.
Single deterministic lookup permutation; no cold-cache, adversarial collision, allocator fragmentation/RSS, application trace, or multithread performance claim.
Population 1 allocation/resize/free measures one operation per process and is noisy; its resize median regressed.
Population 1024 allocation median regressed approximately 4.7%; retain it rather than claiming every phase wins.
Separate chaining is expected constant-time with good distribution, not worst-case constant-time. Resize still holds heap mutex.
The stats struct has an added field; callers must be rebuilt with the experimental library.
Discord roadmap is future scope; no libc-free runtime or Discord implementation delivered.

independent_reviews.correctness: PASS: hash invariants, lock discipline, cleanup and accounting
independent_reviews.edge_cases: PASS: independent fault-injection test and audit
independent_reviews.benchmark: PASS: recomputed phase statistics and checked source/object/binary hashes, scope and relocation links
